frameworks.name: Agentic RAG for Email
frameworks.definition: A reusable method that combines retrieval, multi-step reasoning (planning), and controlled action to turn a mailbox into an assistant that can triage, draft, and execute email tasks.
steps: Ingest and incrementally sync mailbox content into a searchable corpus.
Parse emails (strip signatures/quoted history) and chunk for coherent retrieval units, storing thread and sender metadata.
Create a hybrid index (vector + keyword) and expose a filtered retriever that returns grounded snippets with metadata.
Wrap retrieval as a tool the planner can call; give the agent clear action tools (draft, send, label) with explicit constraints.
Run the agent loop: plan (decide whether to search), retrieve evidence, generate an action or reply, and execute or hand off for approval.
Monitor outputs, log decisions and retrieved evidence, and iterate prompts and retrieval filters to reduce errors.
frameworks.when_to_use: When you need an assistant that not only finds past messages but can plan multi-step workflows and perform limited actions (triage, draft, send) with auditability.
failure_modes: Hallucinated replies not grounded in retrieved email snippets.
Over-permissioning leading to unintended sends or data exposure.
Stale or insufficient metadata causing wrong-thread reconstruction.
Insufficient audit trails that prevent tracing an agent decision.

frameworks.name: Hybrid Index + Governance Framework
frameworks.definition: A governance-first approach that treats indexing, metadata, and action controls as primary design elements to reduce risk when deploying agentic email assistants.
steps: Design an index schema capturing message id, thread id, sender/recipient metadata, received date, labels, and content vectors.
Enable hybrid retrieval (vector similarity + keyword) and provide filters to restrict searches by mailbox, date, or category.
Define allowed agent actions and enforce action caps (which actions are automated vs require approval).
Instrument strong logging, evidence collection (snippets used for generation), and human-review hooks for sensitive outputs.
Establish retention, purge, and access-review policies for email vectors and logs, aligned to compliance needs.
Continuously test with a sandbox dataset, run red-team prompts, and tune retrieval prompts and filters before wider rollout.
frameworks.when_to_use: For production deployments that access sensitive mailboxes or perform automated actions where compliance, privacy, and traceability are required.
failure_modes: Insufficient metadata design leading to irrelevant or risky retrievals.
Weak approval workflows allowing unsafe automated sends.
Incomplete logging making incident investigation impossible.
Misconfiguration of filters exposing cross-tenant or cross-role data.

playbooks.title: Prototype an agentic RAG assistant for Outlook mail
playbooks.trigger: You want a working prototype that can surface relevant past messages and draft/send replies for a focused use case (e.g., invoice queries).
steps: Define scope and allowed actions (read-only search vs. draft/send allowed) and identify a small pilot mailbox or test accounts.
Obtain user/admin consent for mailbox access via enterprise identity; configure incremental sync or change notifications to avoid full reprocessing.
Implement parsing rules (signature removal, strip quoted history) and chunking strategy; persist thread and sender metadata for reconstruction.
Build a hybrid index (vector + keyword) and store relevant metadata for filtered retrieval.
Wrap retrieval as a callable tool the agent can use; design a concise system prompt that requires grounding in retrieved snippets.
Run the agent in read-only mode to validate retrievals and generated drafts; capture evidence and refine retrieval prompts.
Enable send-action only behind a human-in-the-loop approval step; iterate on edge cases before expanding permissions.
playbooks.applicable_when: When you need a quick but safe demo to validate retrieval quality and end-to-end planning before a larger rollout.

playbooks.title: Operationalise and govern an agentic email assistant
playbooks.trigger: After a successful prototype, you need to move to production with compliance, monitoring, and risk controls.
steps: Catalogue regulatory and organisational requirements for email access and automated messaging; map to data retention and audit needs.
Lock down action scopes: define which senders/accounts the agent may act for and design approval gates for outbound messages.
Instrument comprehensive logging: retrieval evidence, prompt inputs, agent plans, and action outcomes for each decision.
Implement monitoring and alerting for anomalous agent behaviour (high send rate, repeated overrides, unusual recipients).
Schedule periodic index refresh and data purges; run regular red-team tests to surface hallucination or privacy leaks.
Define incident response and rollback procedures, including how to revoke agent privileges and remove indexed vectors if needed.
playbooks.applicable_when: When the assistant will be used across teams, handle sensitive information, or perform automated outbound actions.

claims.text: Agents combine retrieval, multi-step reasoning (planning) and action execution to both find relevant messages and perform follow-up tasks like drafting or sending replies.
claims.source_excerpt: Agents combine **retrieval + reasoning + action**. They can plan (“find today’s unread customer escalations”), retrieve (vector search across mail), and then act (draft replies or file tickets) with minimal human hand-holding.

claims.text: Hybrid search—combining vector similarity with keyword (BM25-style) scoring—improves long-tail keyword recall while preserving semantic matching.
claims.source_excerpt: Vector store: Azure AI Search hybrid (vector + BM25) is the path of least resistance; Pinecone/Qdrant work too.

claims.text: Stream change notifications (webhook) from the mailbox provider so each notification can trigger re-chunk, re-embed and an upsert to the index, avoiding full reprocessing of the entire mailbox.
claims.source_excerpt: Create a Graph subscription → webhook/Azure Function. Each notification triggers re-chunk → re-embed → upsert to index.

glossary.one_line: A RAG setup where retrieval, multi-step planning, and limited action execution are combined into an autonomous assistant.
A component that finds and returns relevant documents or snippets from an index to ground generation.
A numerical representation of text that captures semantic meaning for similarity search.
A datastore optimised for similarity search over embeddings, often combined with metadata and keyword indexes.
A search approach that combines vector similarity with keyword scoring to balance semantic and lexical relevance.
A component or prompt that decomposes high-level user goals into ordered retrieval and action steps.
When an LLM generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or unsupported content.

frameworks.name: RAG 2.0 Operational Blueprint
frameworks.definition: A pragmatic, production-oriented pattern that separates ingestion, embedding, vector storage, retrieval+re-ranking, and LLM/agent services to scale retrieval-augmented systems safely.
steps: Treat ingestion as a background process that writes canonical messages and metadata to a durable store.
Run embeddings in a dedicated worker, persist vectors alongside metadata in a vector store.
Serve retrieval via a stateless retriever service that returns a top-k set.
Apply a lightweight re-ranker to the top-k results before passing the final context to the LLM/agent service.
Expose a small API for UI and bot front-ends and autoscale retrieval/generation independently.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a prototype RAG app needs to scale beyond small datasets, support concurrent users, or reduce latency and operational coupling.
failure_modes: Over-partitioning too early, causing unnecessary operational overhead for small teams.
Poorly maintained metadata leading to ineffective filtering and degraded retrieval quality.
Not instrumenting latency/throughput, so bottlenecks (embeddings, re-ranking, LLM) remain invisible.

frameworks.name: Incremental Performance-First Upgrade
frameworks.definition: A prioritized, low-risk sequence of surgical changes that meaningfully reduce latency and cost while preserving the existing architecture.
steps: Benchmark current latencies and identify the heaviest phases (index load, embedding calls, model inference).
Introduce lazy index loading and on-disk memory mapping to reduce cold-start overhead.
Add an on-disk embedding cache to avoid repeat embeddings and reduce external model calls.
Insert a lightweight re-ranking stage after initial retrieval to improve context quality without changing the LLM.
Make inference calls non-blocking for front-ends (run heavy calls off the request thread) and add scoped filtering to narrow searches.
frameworks.when_to_use: When you must improve responsiveness and cost within days or weeks without a full re-architecture.
failure_modes: Cache staleness or invalidation gaps when ingestion continues without coordinated cache invalidation.
Added complexity (re-ranker, cache) without observability, making regressions hard to diagnose.
Partial rollout causing inconsistent behavior between UI endpoints if changes aren’t applied uniformly.

playbooks.title: Week-long RAG Performance Sprint
playbooks.trigger: App exhibits high cold-start time, frequent re-embedding, or user-visible latency under modest load.
steps: Run end-to-end benchmarks to capture cold-start, retrieval, re-ranking and LLM latencies and cost profile.
Implement lazy loading/memory-mapped index to reduce cold-start time and memory footprint.
Add an on-disk embedding cache to avoid repeat embedding calls; measure cache hit-rate.
Add a lightweight re-ranking stage to the retrieval path and compare answer quality on representative queries.
Make inference non-blocking for front-ends so UIs remain responsive; monitor error/timeout rates.
Prune duplicate/legacy ingestion paths to avoid accidental double-builds and index thrash.
Validate improvements with A/B tests or representative query sets and roll changes to production.
playbooks.applicable_when: You need fast, measurable improvements in latency and cost within a short engineering sprint and cannot undertake a full refactor.

playbooks.title: Three-Service RAG Migration Playbook
playbooks.trigger: Project needs to move from a monolith to a scalable deployment that supports growth in messages, users, and index rebuild frequency.
steps: Design service boundaries: ingestion worker, embedding worker, and retrieval/LLM API.
Migrate raw messages to a durable relational store and persist embeddings/metadata to a vector store.
Introduce a background job system to decouple ingestion and embedding from user-facing services.
Expose a small, well-instrumented API for retrieval and generation; autoscale services independently.
Add observability: latency metrics per stage, cache hit/miss rates, and error budgets for inference.
playbooks.applicable_when: You anticipate growth beyond prototype scale (large datasets, concurrent users) and need operational resilience and independent scaling.

claims.text: The existing design is adequate for a few thousand messages and low traffic but is not optimal once you exceed ~100,000 messages, concurrent users, or frequent index rebuilds.
claims.source_excerpt: the design works for a few thousand messages and low traffic, but it is not optimal once you cross (a) > 100 k messages, (b) concurrent users, or (c) frequent index rebuilds.

claims.text: Keeping a large vector index fully resident in-process causes slow cold starts and substantial memory pressure on low-RAM hosts when the index is gigabytes in size.
claims.source_excerpt: FAISS index is kept in RAM inside the bot process; every cold start triggers a load of ≥ 1 GB → slow start, memory pressure on low-RAM hosts.

claims.text: Adding an on-disk embedding cache typically cuts repeat embedding requests by more than 80% in normal usage patterns, reducing cost and latency.
claims.source_excerpt: Add an on-disk embedding cache... Cuts embedding requests by > 80 % in typical usage → cheaper & faster.

claims.text: Introducing a lightweight re-ranker after initial vector retrieval can improve retrieval quality by roughly 10–15% F1, producing noticeably better answers without extra LLM calls.
claims.source_excerpt: +10-15 F1 retrieval accuracy → noticeably better answers with zero LLM cost.

glossary.one_line: A pattern where an LLM augments its context with retrieved documents to ground generation in source data.
A database optimized for storing and searching dense numeric vectors used for semantic retrieval.
A numeric vector representation of text that captures semantic meaning for similarity search.
A component that finds candidate documents from a vector store or corpus to provide context for generation.
A secondary scorer that reranks an initial candidate set to improve final retrieval quality before generation.
The maximum amount of text an LLM can effectively condition on when generating a response.
An orchestrated LLM workflow that can use tools, retrieval, and multi-step reasoning to complete tasks.
When an LLM produces plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or unsupported information.

frameworks.name: Marco de cuatro ámbitos para evaluación concesional
frameworks.definition: Estructura integrada que considera (1) marco legal/institucional, (2) contabilidad y efecto fiscal, (3) mercado/financiación y (4) viabilidad técnica/costos para juzgar la idoneidad de un proyecto vial para concesión/PPP.
steps: Revisar normativa aplicable (Directiva 2014/23/UE, LCSP 2017, Leyes sectoriales) y jurisprudencia relevante.
Evaluar impacto contable y fiscal (criterios SEC-2010; posible entrada en balance pública).
Analizar demanda y riesgos de ingresos (tráfico, pago por uso, externalidades de sostenibilidad).
Valorar viabilidad técnica y estimación de CAPEX/OPEX; calcular VFM (valor por dinero) para la administración.
Diseñar asignación de riesgos contractual y mecanismos de revisión (equilibrio económico-financiero, cláusulas de ajuste).
Probar escenarios financieros y jurídicos (stress tests) y concluir recomendación estratégica.
frameworks.when_to_use: Evaluación estratégica inicial de cualquier proyecto vial en España cuando se decide si promoverlo por concesión/PPP o vía pública.
failure_modes: Análisis jurídico incompleto que ignora criterios SEC-2010 o jurisprudencia europea.
Subestimación del riesgo de demanda o garantías implícitas que invalidan la transferencia real de riesgo.
Diseño contractual con mecanismos de revisión que devuelven el riesgo al sector público.
Omisión de efectos macroeconómicos (p. ej., desindexación) que deterioran la viabilidad financiera.

frameworks.name: Checklist de transferencia de riesgo y contabilidad SEC
frameworks.definition: Lista operativa para verificar que una concesión transfiere riesgos de forma suficiente y cumple los requisitos para no computar como deuda pública según SEC-2010.
steps: Identificar y mapear todos los riesgos del proyecto (construcción, disponibilidad, demanda, demanda residual, operativo).
Asignar responsable contractual de cada riesgo y documentar evidencia de exposición real a incertidumbres de mercado.
Detectar garantías, mínimos de tráfico o mecanismos de cobertura que puedan reducir la exposición privada.
Evaluar si la estructura financiera y las cláusulas permiten considerar la deuda fuera de balance según SEC-2010.
Redactar o ajustar cláusulas para asegurar transferencia efectiva de riesgos sin crear ayudas encubiertas.
Someter a revisión independiente (auditor fiscal/jurídico) antes de la aprobación política.
frameworks.when_to_use: Al diseñar o revisar la estructura financiera y contractual de una concesión cuando el objetivo es limitar el impacto fiscal y evitar reclasificación contable.

playbooks.title: Evaluación estratégica de viabilidad concesional (nivel ejecutivo)
playbooks.trigger: Decisión inicial sobre si promover o licitar una carretera mediante concesión/PPP.
steps: Recolectar contexto legal, institucional y político relevante para la vía y la administración promotora.
Aplicar el Marco de cuatro ámbitos para valorar encaje legal, fiscal, mercado y técnica.
Modelizar escenarios de demanda y estados financieros (ingresos por peaje, pagos por disponibilidad, sensibilidad a variables clave).
Comprobar criterios SEC-2010 y el posible tratamiento en balance público.
Formular opciones de asignación de riesgo y mecanismos contractuales (incluyendo restablecimiento del equilibrio).
Proponer recomendación ejecutiva: concesión pura, concesión con ajustes, colaboración público-privada híbrida o provisión pública.
playbooks.applicable_when: Cuando una autoridad pública, inversor o asesor debe decidir la vía contractual óptima para una infraestructura vial en España.

playbooks.title: Negociación de cláusulas de equilibrio económico y ajuste por costes
playbooks.trigger: Negociación de un contrato concesional a largo plazo sujeto a riesgo inflacionario y variaciones de costes.
steps: Identificar eventos que justifiquen restablecimiento del equilibrio (cambios regulatorios, competencia nueva, shock macro).
Diseñar fórmulas objetivas de ajuste que respeten la Ley 2/2015 de Desindexación (mecanismos no automáticos vinculados a índices relevantes).
Limitar garantías y topes que puedan convertir la concesión en ayuda estatal encubierta o hacerla on-balance.
Incluir procedimientos de verificación, auditoría independiente y métodos de resolución de disputas.
Stress-test contractual con escenarios extremos y acordar triggers y antiutillaje (cláusulas de salida y compensación medible).
playbooks.applicable_when: Al redactar o renegociar contratos concesionales donde los cambios de costes a largo plazo y la protección fiscal son críticamente relevantes.

claims.text: La Directiva 2014/23/UE exige transferencia efectiva del riesgo operacional al concesionario como rasgo definitorio del contrato de concesión.
claims.source_excerpt: La Directiva 2014/23/UE ... exige la transferencia efectiva del riesgo operacional al concesionario como rasgo definitorio.

claims.text: El Manual SEC-2010 establece que una concesión queda fuera del balance público solo si el socio privado asume la mayor parte de los riesgos de construcción y disponibilidad/demanda.
claims.source_excerpt: El Manual SEC-2010 señala que la deuda de la concesión no computará como pública excepto si la Administración financia la mayor parte... o garantiza más del 50% de la deuda.

claims.text: La Ley 2/2015 de Desindexación prohíbe la indexación automática de contratos públicos al IPC, afectando la actualización de peajes y cánones en concesiones.
claims.source_excerpt: La Ley 2/2015 de Desindexación ... prohíbe la indexación automática de contratos públicos a la inflación.

claims.text: La Responsabilidad Patrimonial de la Administración (RPA) puede obligar a indemnizar si una concesión se resuelve anticipadamente por causas no imputables al concesionario.
claims.source_excerpt: La figura de la Responsabilidad Patrimonial de la Administración (RPA) ... ha generado obligaciones de pago del Estado si la concesión se resuelve anticipadamente.

glossary.one_line: Contrato público donde una administración confiere a un privado la explotación y/o construcción de obra, con transferencia de riesgos y contraprestación.
Criterio por el que el concesionario asume incertidumbres de explotación (demanda, ingresos, costes operativos).
Manual europeo de contabilidad pública que determina cuándo una PPP/concesión computa como deuda pública.
Norma española que limita la indexación automática de precios y contratos públicos a la inflación.
Obligación de la Administración de resarcir daños ocasionados por el funcionamiento público, aplicable en resoluciones de concesiones.
Cláusula contractual para ajustar condiciones de la concesión cuando cambios externos alteran la rentabilidad pactada.
Mecanismo de ingresos basado en el cobro directo al usuario por el uso de la infraestructura.
Situación donde una concesión contiene garantías o beneficios que equivalen a una subvención pública contraria a normas UE.

frameworks.name: RAG System Audit Framework
frameworks.definition: A structured, non-invasive method to diagnose Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems by mapping topology, validating data flows, and prioritising fixes.
steps: Map repository structure and annotate each module's prime responsibility.
Trace execution paths from main entry points to identify exercised vs dormant modules.
Validate embedding and vector-store consistency (dimensions, index paths, index update calls).
Cross-check agent/tool metadata against actual callable implementations.
Run static analysis (linters, type-checker, tests) and collect errors into a findings register.
Classify issues by severity and produce a prioritized remediation backlog with quick fixes first.
frameworks.when_to_use: Use when a RAG-enabled app shows degraded performance, runtime errors, or unexpected behaviour after incremental development.
failure_modes: Dynamic imports or runtime codegen hide dependencies from static checks, producing false negatives.
Large monolithic modules make tracing expensive and obscure the true failure point.
Insufficient test coverage prevents confident refactoring after fixes.

frameworks.name: Agent Tool-Registration Verification Framework
frameworks.definition: A compact method to verify that declared agent tools are properly implemented and reachable at runtime (metadata ↔ implementation ↔ agent).
steps: Extract declared tools from agent metadata files and list expected signatures.
Locate corresponding implementations in tools modules and note export names.
Determine how the agent imports/instantiates tools (static import, registry, dynamic import).
Flag mismatches: metadata-only, impl-only, name/signature differences, or missing registration calls.
Recommend fixes: restore missing imports, update metadata to reflect actual API, or merge duplicate implementations.
frameworks.when_to_use: When an LLM/agent reports missing tools, fails tool-calls, or when a repo contains multiple tool implementations and metadata files.
failure_modes: Agent uses dynamic discovery (strings, eval) making static mapping incomplete.
Multiple similarly named tools across modules produce ambiguous matches.
Tool signatures evolve without metadata updates, causing runtime invocation errors.

playbooks.title: Non-invasive Repository Audit for a RAG App
playbooks.trigger: App exhibits runtime errors, under-performance, or you suspect duplicated/legacy code from copilot-driven development.
steps: Create an artifacts folder to collect analysis outputs and keep the working repo untouched.
Produce a module map listing every Python file and its prime responsibility.
Trace call paths for every main entry (UI, bot, batch pipeline) to surface dormant modules.
Cross-check agent metadata vs tool implementations and validate embedding/index usage.
Run static-analysis tools and tests, saving raw outputs into the artifacts folder.
Aggregate findings into two deliverables: a repo map and a prioritized inconsistencies list.
playbooks.applicable_when: You need a repeatable, low-risk diagnostic deliverable before approving code changes or refactors.

playbooks.title: Executive Remediation Plan after Audit
playbooks.trigger: Audit delivers a prioritized list of inconsistencies requiring staged fixes and stakeholder buy-in.
steps: Group findings into High/Medium/Low severity and estimate quick-fix effort for each high-severity item.
Propose an order of operations that isolates high-risk production fixes from low-risk refactors.
Assign owners and short time-boxed workstreams for critical items (hotfix, validation, monitor).
Define success criteria for each fix (e.g., tests passing, reduced error rate, consistent index state).
Prepare a one-page executive summary with estimated cost/risk and the recommended next three sprint tasks.
playbooks.applicable_when: After a technical audit that requires cross-functional coordination (engineering, ops, product, stakeholders).

claims.text: Incremental development assisted by code copilots commonly produces duplicated modules and metadata drift that lead to disconnected functionality.
claims.source_excerpt: long, incremental process of code development using a cursor copilot that may have disconnected modules or created misconfigurations.

claims.text: Static analysis (linters, strict type-checking and running tests) is an effective first step to discover dead imports, typing errors and failing tests before runtime debugging.
claims.source_excerpt: Static analysis first (AST parsing, regex, importlib); no need to run the bot or Streamlit.

claims.text: Redirect errors that report missing output files typically indicate the target directory for captured logs does not exist; creating the directory resolves the redirection failure.
claims.source_excerpt: zsh: no such file or directory: architecture/… just means the folder you’re trying to write into doesn’t exist yet.

frameworks.name: Part-time High‑Value Advisory Packaging Framework
frameworks.definition: A repeatable approach to convert senior infrastructure/PPP expertise into short, high-margin engagements and semi-passive products while capping weekly hours.
steps: Set precise time vs money targets (ceiling on billable days, revenue goal, required day‑rate).
Select highest-value, low-time services (expert calls, short DD, board roles, masterclasses, licensing).
Sharpen positioning and brand (niche headline, two‑page CV, targeted thought leadership).
Build a low‑maintenance route to market (expert networks, brokers, direct client outreach, board recruiters).
Adopt a three‑tier pricing menu and master services agreement with upfront/retainer mechanics.
Operationalise for limited hours (VA, templates, standard NDAs/MSAs, basic automation).
Launch upside levers (cohort courses, paid newsletter, equity/carry where appropriate).
Implement risk & lifestyle guardrails (travel limits, runway, utilisation-based rate reviews).
frameworks.when_to_use: When an experienced PPP/infrastructure professional wants to reduce active hours (~15–20/week) while maintaining or increasing income.
failure_modes: Underpricing: day‑rate too low relative to market reduces feasibility.
Insufficient pipeline: not securing repeat or platform-sourced engagements.
Scope creep: weak contracts or no time‑cap clauses lead to overwork.
Poor productisation: bespoke work not converted to repeatable offers, raising time intensity.

frameworks.name: Three‑Tier Pricing & Contract Guardrail Framework
frameworks.definition: A compact pricing and contracting system that simplifies negotiations, protects time boundaries, and accelerates client decisions for fractional advisors.
steps: Define 2–4 fixed tiers (e.g., expert call, short DD, retainer/NED) with clear deliverables and rates.
Require simple payment mechanics (upfront for calls, 50% on project kickoff, monthly for retainers).
Embed time‑cap clauses so overruns become change orders.
Use a short master services agreement + standard NDA to speed onboarding.
Review utilisation and raise rates annually when utilisation exceeds a threshold.
frameworks.when_to_use: When selling short, high‑value advisory services and accepting board or retainer work where quick contracting and clear boundaries matter.
failure_modes: Client pushback on upfront payments or fixed tiers slowing deal flow.
Ambiguous deliverables causing disputes and unpaid overruns.
Failure to enforce time caps resulting in creeping workload.
Not updating rates leads to erosion of premium positioning.

playbooks.title: Pivot to Part‑Time High‑Fee Advisory (15–20 hrs/week)
playbooks.trigger: You want to reduce active hours and replace or exceed full‑time income using your senior PPP/infrastructure expertise.
steps: Set a clear annual revenue target and max billable days to compute a required day‑rate.
Choose a small menu of high‑value services (expert calls, short red‑flag DDs, NEDs, masterclasses, licensing).
Refresh LinkedIn, shorten CV to two pages, craft a niche headline, and plan quarterly thought leadership.
Register on expert‑network platforms and specialist brokerages; notify 20–30 warm contacts of availability.
Publish templates (DD memo, board deck) and assemble standard NDA/MSA documents.
Adopt a three‑tier pricing menu with upfront and retainer payment mechanics and time‑cap clauses.
Hire a virtual assistant for admin, automate simple lead capture, and set travel/availability guardrails.
Monitor utilisation and pipeline; iterate offers and rates annually.
playbooks.applicable_when: Experienced advisors with an established track record in PPP/project finance who can monetise expertise in short engagements.

playbooks.title: Rapid Expert‑Call & Short Diligence Productisation
playbooks.trigger: You want quick, low‑time revenue from expert networks and short institutional reviews without becoming full‑time.
steps: Create a condensed, issue‑focused CV tailored to expert networks and platforms.
Standardise a 60–90 minute expert‑call product with a short prep pack and flat fee.
Package a one‑to‑two day 'red‑flag' diligence product using templated memos and a fixed price.
Use a short MSA/NDA and require upfront payment or confirmed platform payment.
Limit travel and add explicit time‑caps to engagements; convert repeat clients to retainer or board talks.
Track conversion metrics and reuse calls into paid masterclasses or newsletter content.
playbooks.applicable_when: When you need to monetise domain knowledge quickly and prefer predictable, low‑time commitments.

frameworks.name: ToR-to-Proposal Framework
frameworks.definition: A repeatable method for converting a client's Terms of Reference into a structured services proposal that aligns scope, methodology, team, timeline and budget.
steps: Clarify the assignment and desired deliverables from the ToR
Extract and map key requirements, constraints, and success criteria
Define proposal structure (Objectives, Scope, Methodology, Team, Workplan, Budget, References)
Draft each section tailored to the client's priorities and language
Surface assumptions, exclusions and risk allocation
Quality-check for alignment with ToR and procurement/compliance requirements
frameworks.when_to_use: When preparing a technical and/or financial services proposal in response to a client's Terms of Reference.
failure_modes: Misreading or omitting key ToR requirements (scope mismatch)
Failing to state assumptions or exclusions clearly
Budget or timeline inconsistent with described scope
Tone or format incompatible with client procurement rules

frameworks.name: Six-Strategy Prompt Design Framework
frameworks.definition: A structured approach to craft prompts using six complementary strategies to improve clarity, relevance and reproducibility of model outputs.
steps: Write clear, unambiguous instructions describing the task and goal
Provide reference text or the relevant excerpt (e.g., the ToR)
Split complex tasks into simpler subtasks (analyze, outline, draft, refine)
Give examples or few-shot samples of the desired output
Specify the desired format (headings, JSON, table, length, tone)
Experiment with variations and iterate based on test outputs
frameworks.when_to_use: When designing prompts for tasks that require reliable, repeatable outputs — for example, drafting structured proposals from client documents.
failure_modes: Overly broad instructions leading to generic or irrelevant outputs
Missing reference material so the model hallucinates details
Too-complex single-step prompts that the model fails to decompose
Undefined output format causing inconsistent or unusable results

playbooks.title: Draft a Services Proposal from a Terms of Reference
playbooks.trigger: Receive a client's Terms of Reference and need to submit a compliant proposal.
steps: Read the ToR fully and highlight explicit deliverables, timelines, and evaluation criteria
Summarize the client's objectives and constraints in one paragraph
Map ToR requirements to proposal sections (Objectives, Scope, Methodology, Team, Timeline, Budget)
Draft the Methodology and Workplan to show how each ToR requirement will be met
Assemble CVs and relevant experience that match evaluation criteria
Produce a clear budget/fee structure linked to deliverables and milestones
Add assumptions, exclusions and risk mitigation
Review for alignment with ToR language, procurement rules and required formats
Iterate after internal review or client clarifications
playbooks.applicable_when: When preparing a bid or services proposal to respond directly to a client's ToR, especially under formal procurement processes.

playbooks.title: Test and Refine a Prompt Template for Proposal Drafting
playbooks.trigger: After creating an initial prompt or template to generate proposals from ToRs and you need to improve reliability and fidelity.
steps: Run the prompt against a real or sample ToR to produce an initial draft
Evaluate the output for completeness, fidelity to ToR, tone and format
Identify recurring errors or omissions and adjust instructions, examples or format constraints
Introduce or refine few-shot examples to steer structure and language
Break the job into subtasks (analyze ToR → outline → draft sections) if single-step output is poor
Repeat testing with representative ToRs and keep a changelog of prompt versions
Create acceptance criteria or a simple rubric to judge outputs automatically or by reviewers
playbooks.applicable_when: When you want consistent, high-quality proposal drafts from an LLM and need an auditable process for prompt improvement.
